t: Ghidra: What Ghidra Is: The Disassembler That Reads for You
title: Ghidra: What Ghidra Is: The Disassembler That Reads for You
description: Ghidra is the free, open-source reverse-engineering suite released by the NSA in 2019: it disassembles machine code for dozens of architectures, decompiles it to readable C-like pseudocode, and provides scripted analysis (Java/Python) over the program database. Analysts use it to understand firmware they own, find vulnerabilities in their own code, and dissect malware to build defenses. The decompiler is the star — reading assembly is slow; reading Ghidra's decompilation is merely hard.

t: Ghidra: The Decompiler: From Bytes to Logic
title: Ghidra: The Decompiler: From Bytes to Logic
description: Ghidra's decompiler lifts assembly to structured pseudocode: control flow recovered, variables named (by you), types applied. It is not perfect — optimized code confuses it — but it turns weeks of assembly reading into days of pseudocode reading. The skill is guiding it: naming functions, defining structs, marking up the unknown until the logic emerges. Decompilation is a conversation between the analyst and the tool.
key_facts: Analyst guides with names and types

t: Ghidra: Firmware Analysis: Your Own Devices
title: Ghidra: Firmware Analysis: Your Own Devices
description: The primary defensive use: analyzing firmware of devices you own — extracting filesystems (binwalk-style), finding hardcoded credentials, auditing update mechanisms, verifying the vendor's security claims. Ghidra loads the raw binary at the right base address, finds the code, and the analyst hunts for the vulnerability before the adversary does. Every finding becomes a patch or a procurement decision.

t: Ghidra: Malware Analysis: Learning the Enemy's Playbook
title: Ghidra: Malware Analysis: Learning the Enemy's Playbook
description: Defensive malware analysis dissects captured samples to build defenses: what does it do, how does it persist, what are its indicators? Ghidra's decompiler plus dynamic analysis (sandbox detonation) reveals the playbook; the indicators become detection rules. The work is defensive by purpose — understand the attack to build the defense — conducted in isolated labs with strict handling. Never analyze malware to improve it.

t: Ghidra: Your First Binary: Strings to Main
title: Ghidra: Your First Binary: Strings to Main
description: The hello-world: load a small binary, run auto-analysis, check the strings window for the interesting literals, find main, read the decompilation. The strings are the map — URLs, paths, error messages lead to the code that matters. From there: rename functions, define the key structs, follow the cross-references. The first binary teaches the loop: explore, hypothesize, verify in the decompiler.

title: Ghidra: Scripting: Automating the Analysis
description: Ghidra's scripting (GhidraScript Java, plus Python) automates the repetitive: find all crypto constants, list all network calls, rename by pattern, diff two firmware versions. The script library is institutional knowledge — the team's hard-won patterns, runnable. Writing a script that finds your product's bug class across every firmware version is leverage no manual analysis matches.

t: Ghidra: Loaders and Processor Modules: New Architectures
title: Ghidra: Loaders and Processor Modules: New Architectures
description: Ghidra's architecture support is extensible: loaders parse new binary formats, processor modules (SLEIGH specifications) describe new instruction sets. When the team meets an exotic chip — custom DSP, new microcontroller — writing the SLEIGH spec brings it into the analysis world. The skill is rare and decisive: the team that can describe the processor can analyze anything built on it.

t: Ghidra: Diffing: What Changed Between Versions
title: Ghidra: Diffing: What Changed Between Versions
description: Version diffing compares two firmware builds: which functions changed, what was added, what was patched. For defenders, diffing the vendor's security update reveals what was fixed (and hints at what was vulnerable); diffing your own builds verifies the patch. Ghidra's Version Tracking does the structural matching. The discipline is diffing every update that touches security-relevant code.

t: Ghidra: Defensive Uses: The Vulnerability Program
title: Ghidra: Defensive Uses: The Vulnerability Program

Reverse engineering is the deep end of defensive analysis: slow, skilled, and decisive where it counts.

title: Ghidra: Collaboration: Team Reverse Engineering
description: Ghidra's server mode lets teams share a program database: one analyst names the network code, another the crypto, the merge keeps both. Large binaries (OS kernels, complex firmware) are team efforts, and the shared database is the collective understanding. The discipline is markup hygiene — named functions, typed structs, commented reasoning — so the next analyst inherits understanding, not confusion.

t: Ghidra: Debugging: When the Decompiler Lies
title: Ghidra: Debugging: When the Decompiler Lies
description: The decompiler misleads: optimized code, indirect jumps, obfuscation. The defense is the disassembly — when the pseudocode looks wrong, read the assembly it came from. Cross-references (who calls this? who reads this string?) ground the hypotheses. And dynamic analysis (debugger, emulator) arbitrates: run it, watch what it does. Static proposes; dynamic disposes.

t: Ghidra: Testing: Validating Your Own Defenses
title: Ghidra: Testing: Validating Your Own Defenses

t: Ghidra: Real-World Pattern: Fleet Firmware Audit
title: Ghidra: Real-World Pattern: Fleet Firmware Audit
description: A complete pattern: an organization audits the firmware of its deployed device fleet — extract, analyze, find hardcoded credentials in two models, notify vendors, patch one, mitigate the other with network controls, verify by diffing the patched firmware. The audit repeats annually. The fleet's firmware is no longer a black box; it is a reviewed artifact.
